title: At the Swimming Pool
description: Explore a pool through familiar swimming words, equipment, and the places around the water.
cardDescription: Explore a pool through familiar swimming words, equipment, and the places around the water.
focus: The clues identify movements and objects by their purpose. They provide vocabulary rather than a swimming lesson.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for an action, a place, or an item used beside the pool.
words: To move through water using the body
Prepared basin containing water for swimming
Marked strip of pool space used by a swimmer
One length or circuit counted during swimming
Repeated arm-and-body action used to swim
To remain supported at the water’s surface
To move the legs to help propel the body in water
To move smoothly through water without a new stroke
Protective lenses worn over the eyes while swimming
Absorbent cloth used after leaving a pool
Close-fitting head covering worn by a swimmer
Runged structure used to climb out of a pool
Boundary around the top of a pool

answerNotes.STROKE: A swimming stroke is a repeated pattern of body and arm movement. It is an action rather than a counted length of the pool.
answerNotes.LANE: A lane is a marked route within the pool. It helps distinguish one swimmer’s space from another.
answerNotes.GOGGLES: Goggles is a plural-form word for protective eyewear. The clue refers to the pair rather than one lens.
answerNotes.LAP: Lap is used for a counted swimming length or circuit. Usage varies, so the clue allows both common meanings.

title: Around the Running Track
description: Follow a track through familiar race stages, distances, and objects passed between runners.
cardDescription: Follow a track through familiar race stages, distances, and objects passed between runners.
focus: The clues describe running vocabulary without requiring a speed or training plan. Actions and units of play have distinct meanings.
solvingTip: Look for a stage, a movement, or an item handled during a relay.
words: Marked route used for running races
Contest to complete a route before other participants
To move faster than a walk with a running gait
To travel on foot without running
To run at a gentle steady pace
One complete circuit of a running track
Marked strip assigned to a runner on a track
Rate at which a person moves along a route
Point or moment at which a race begins
End point of a running race
Race in which teammates complete successive stages
Short stick passed between relay runners
Barrier jumped during a track race

answerNotes.RELAY: A relay divides a race among teammates. Each person completes a stage before the next takes over.
answerNotes.BATON: A baton is the object passed in a relay. The word also names a conductor’s stick in music.
answerNotes.PACE: Pace describes movement rate. The clue asks for a general term rather than a particular speed.
answerNotes.HURDLE: A hurdle is the physical barrier here. The same word can describe an obstacle in an everyday situation.

title: A Bicycle by the Path
description: Look over a bicycle through familiar parts, supports, and equipment used during a ride.
cardDescription: Look over a bicycle through familiar parts, supports, and equipment used during a ride.
focus: The clues identify what a bicycle part does or where it sits. Knowing the shape or job is enough to enter the grid.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue describes a wheel part, a control, or a supporting structure.
words: Foot-operated part that drives a bicycle
Linked metal loop transmitting pedaling power
Drive setting selected to change pedaling effort on a bicycle
Device used to slow a bicycle wheel
Circular assembly turning beneath a bicycle
Thin support running between a wheel’s hub and rim
Rubber outer covering around a bicycle wheel
Inflatable inner part used inside many bicycle tires
Steering bar gripped by a cyclist
Protective head covering used by a cyclist
Main supporting structure joining bicycle parts
Small ringing device fitted to some handlebars

answerNotes.SADDLE: Saddle means the bicycle seat here. It is not riding equipment placed on a horse.
answerNotes.SPOKE: A spoke connects the hub and rim. It is one support rather than the whole wheel.
answerNotes.TIRE: Tire is the American spelling for the rubber covering. Tyre is a common British spelling.
answerNotes.FRAME: The frame is the main supporting structure. The clue asks for that whole structure rather than one rotating part.

title: Table Tennis at the Club
description: Explore table tennis through familiar equipment and the words used for serving, bouncing, and returning the ball.
cardDescription: Explore table tennis through familiar equipment and the words used for serving, bouncing, and returning the ball.
focus: The clues define the sport’s objects and common actions. A few short words identify particular kinds of shots.
solvingTip: Look for a playing object, a movement, or a result of contact with the table.
words: Handheld striking implement used in table tennis
Small light sphere hit across a table-tennis net
Low mesh barrier across the center of the table
Raised flat playing surface carrying the net in a paddle-and-ball game
Play that sends the ball into action at the start of a rally
Series of returns exchanged in table tennis
Rotation put on a table-tennis ball
Topspin attacking stroke in table tennis
To rebound after striking the table
Outer boundary of the playing tabletop
Points recorded for the sides in a game
One contest forming part of a table-tennis match
Format with two table-tennis players on each side

answerNotes.PADDLE: Paddle is a common American name for the striking implement. Racket and bat are also used in table-tennis terminology.
answerNotes.SPIN: Spin names the ball’s rotation. It is separate from how quickly the ball travels forward.
answerNotes.LOOP: A loop is an attacking topspin stroke in this sport. It does not mean a bent length of string here.
answerNotes.DOUBLES: Doubles has two players per side. The name describes the playing format rather than a point value.

title: Badminton in the Hall
description: Meet badminton through familiar court words and descriptions of the shuttle, racket, and basic shots.
cardDescription: Meet badminton through familiar court words and descriptions of the shuttle, racket, and basic shots.
focus: The clues identify equipment and common playing actions. Direct descriptions introduce the light projectile used instead of a ball.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for equipment, a shot, or the number of players on a side.
words: Racket game played by sending a shuttle over a net
Stringed implement used to strike a shuttle
Light conical projectile hit in badminton
One traditional material forming a badminton shuttle’s skirt
Raised barrier across a badminton court
Marked playing area used for badminton
Shot used to start a badminton rally
High deep badminton shot toward the back of the court
Soft shot intended to fall close beyond the net
Format with one badminton player on each side
Format with two badminton players per side
Part of a racket held in the hand

answerNotes.SHUTTLE: Shuttle is short for shuttlecock. Birdie is another familiar name for the light badminton projectile.
answerNotes.CLEAR: A clear is a deep shot in badminton. The clue does not use clear to describe transparent glass.
answerNotes.DROP: A drop shot falls near the net. Its intended placement distinguishes it from a deep clear.
answerNotes.SINGLES: Singles has one player on each side. Doubles uses pairs, so the player count determines the format.
